title: reliquary machine blueprint
description: Synchronized companion to the machine blueprint specification (machine-blueprint.md and machine-blueprint-reference.md), which remains normative. This schema covers the per-document structural subset of the format checks: schema validity never implies blueprint validity — media-name resolution, cross-document rules, and every backend capability check live in the specification only. It validates the parsed document: blueprints accept the JSONC dialect (comments and trailing commas), which is invisible at this level. Blueprints carry no $schema field pre-beta; editors bind this schema to *.rlqb by file association. The machine state (reliquary-machine.json) is a separate document type whose schema lands with the instance-model implementation; its state-only fields are rejected here as unknown keys.

platform.description: The guest platform — the operating-system family the machine is for. Required; never inferred.

backend.description: The virtualization backend hosting the machine. Omitted, the backend is assigned at materialization; declared, it pins the choice and fails rather than falling back.

description.description: Human-readable description. No effect on machine behavior; feeds search. The blueprint's one name is its file stem; there is no display-name field.

scripts.description: Short labels naming scripts (the stem of a .rlqs file). Labels are the verbs used with the script command.

parameters.description: Blueprint-supplied script-input bindings: keys are input names; each value is a direct string value or a {"property": "<key>"} reference into the user property registry. Secret inputs never take direct values (a rule beyond this schema).

property.description: The user-property key the parameter refers to; defined externally in the property registry.

memory.description: Guest memory: a positive integer (MiB) or a size string ("32M"). A size string must resolve to a whole number of MiB — a rule beyond this schema. Defaults by platform.

drives.description: The drive inventory. Keys declare medium and slot (a bare medium name is the slot-0 alias); values declare where the drive's content comes from. Exactly one of media, size, or base per drive object; removable slots (floppy, cdrom) may be null — present hardware with no medium inserted.

boot.description: Boot order: declared, enabled drive keys (canonical or alias form) tried in order. Entries are unique by slot; the mixed alias/indexed spelling of one slot is a rule beyond this schema.

control-planes.description: The ordered control-plane policy: which control planes reliquary may use for this machine, in preference order. Entries are unique. Defaults by platform.

backend-settings.description: The explicitly scoped, non-portable escape hatch: one object per backend name; only the section matching the machine's backend applies. Each backend adapter defines and validates its own section's keys, and rejects overlap with reliquary-owned fields.

sizeString.description: A positive integer immediately followed by a binary unit suffix K, M, G, or T (powers of 1024), case-insensitive.

mediaName.description: The name of a defined media item, resolved from the media catalog. The name grammar is deliberately open pre-asset-spec.

controller.description: The kind of storage controller the drive attaches to — guest-visible hardware, not a backend detail. Default ide.

base.description: A starting-point image the drive's own image is materialized from: a media name (shorthand), or an object with media (required) and type — difference (default: a differencing disk backed by the base) or duplicate (the base copied in full).

oneOf.description: Shorthand: a media-name string, equivalent to an object with only media set.
An empty removable slot: present hardware with no medium inserted.

media.description: Attach the named media payload itself — machine-independent media the machine carries at rest.

size.description: Start the drive as a blank image of this size.

enabled.description: false removes the drive from the machine entirely — no slot, no hardware — while keeping the entry in the document.
